title: Minimum velocity value
description: Essential: The final answer for part (1) must be v1 = 6000 m/s (or 6×10³ m/s).

title: Lorentz force condition
description: Important: Correctly applies the condition qvB = mv²/r for circular motion to relate velocity, magnetic field, and trajectory radius.

title: Geometric tangent condition
description: Important: Identifies that the limiting trajectory for part (1) is a circle of radius r1 = d/2 that is tangent to the x-axis at the origin O.

title: Minimum time value
description: Essential: The final answer for part (2) must be t = (97π/180)×10⁻⁴ s ≈ 1.69×10⁻⁴ s.

title: Time-angle relationship
description: Important: Correctly relates the travel time to the central angle α swept on the circular path, using t = (α/2π)T, where T is the cyclotron period.

title: Geometry for two solutions
description: Important: For part (3), identifies that two distinct initial velocity directions can lead to the same x-intercept, requiring analysis of circle geometry with fixed r and source position S.

title: Segment length value
description: Essential: The final answer for part (3) must be the length MN = 0.22 m or its exact form (2/5)(√7 - √3) m.

title: Incorrect radius calculation
description: Pitfall: Uses an incorrect formula for the cyclotron radius (e.g., r = qB/(mv)) or misapplies the geometric condition r = d/2 for parts (2) or (3).

title: Angle or time unit error
description: Pitfall: Confuses degrees and radians in calculating the central angle or travel time, or incorrectly computes the period T.

title: Sign or direction oversight
description: Pitfall: Fails to account for the negative charge in the force direction or misinterprets the quadrant geometry for the initial velocity angles.
